questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange somewhere with lots of young people, plenty of opportunities in the city, and easy access to travel destinations nearby. It was also important for me to be able to complete my mandatory courses while on exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the necessary information. However, the Italian university system is somewhat slow and bureaucratic, and most of the information was provided shortly before the start of the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received the relevant information via email

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We used Spotahome and had a very good experience. Italianway also appears to be a good website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Book accommodation in advance, and as long as you live within Milan’s city circle, it is easy to get around by bus, metro, or tram.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was possible to register for a wide range of mandatory courses. Although many of the courses overlapped in the timetable, it was manageable, as attendance was not required every time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Most of the relevant information was available on the university’s website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We were able to register for most of our mandatory courses. It was also possible to change courses during the first two weeks of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress too much about course selection, as there is flexibility at the beginning of the semester and it is possible to switch courses during the first weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The overall academic level was lower compared to UCPH. The exams were significantly easier, lasted a maximum of one hour, and consisted of only a few handwritten questions on paper.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more traditional and old-fashioned. However, all lecture slides and course materials were available on the university’s website. There were no assignments, which resulted in a lower workload.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Our rental required weekly cleaning, which cost around €20 per time. Some students experienced higher costs.
Gym was very expensive, around 700-1100 dkk

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks were generally cheap. A cappuccino cost around €1–2, and a pasta was €12–15. Train tickets and flights were also relatively cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many Erasmus-organized events available, including social gatherings and trips. However, we did not participate much in these, as we had already met many Danish students early on and therefore spent most of our time with them. The city also offers a wide range of sports activities, gyms, and several public swimming pools located in the city center.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Milan is centrally located in Europe, making it very easy to travel by train to several cities. The train system is easy to use and relatively cheap. I would therefore recommend traveling to nearby cities and regions, as well as exploring Milan itself. The many museums, bars, cafés, and restaurants.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend using weekends to travel to places such as Lake Como, the Dolomites, Portofino, Naples, and Rome. Milan also has great shopping and vintage markets, cultural events and partying

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust. There were many exchange students, and the culture is not very different from the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participating in social activities, visiting cafes and bars, and interacting with students during classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier, as not everyone speaks English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cafe culture, affordable coffee, aperol and croissants, and the aperitivo tradition.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not stress too much about choosing courses. Remember to experience the city and not spend to much time on schoolwork the exams are easier. Find an apartment early

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Secure accommodation early and be aware that some exams are held in January.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many kind and sweet people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding an apartment with a nice location

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
